title: Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods
summary: On THIS shelf the film is not an outside work — it is where Dragon Ball Super's story starts, in its first telling, and the catalog already says so: lib/rulings/arcs.ts (A46, Sean 2026-08-28) stores the run's opening arc as { label 'Battle of Gods', kind SHARED, eps 1-14 ↔ ch 1-4 }, with the note 'Both tellings descend from the 2013 film 『神と神』'. The owner's instrument is Toyotarou's DRAGON BALL超 manga (AniList 86508, 原作 鳥山明 / 漫画 とよたろう, V-Jump from 2015-06-20) and its opening arc IS this film: 「破壊神ビルス編」 = 其之一 破壊神の予知夢 / 其之二 悟空の敗北 / 其之三 ビルスの怒り / 其之四 神と神 — ch 1-4, volume 1, 65 pages, 2015-06-20 → 2015-09-19 (Kanzenshuu's manga guide: 'Corresponding: Dragon Ball Super Chapters 01-04 (4 chapters), Page Count: 65 pages'; ja-WP's エピソード table lists the same four titles in vol 1; dragonball.fandom's arc infobox prints 'manga chapters=1-4' and says the saga 'is based around the events depicted in the movie Battle of Gods'; the fourth chapter is literally titled 神と神). DIRECTION IS SETTLED: the film (2013-03-30) precedes chapter 1 by two years and three months and TV ep 1 (2015-07-05) by two years and four, so the manga digests the film and never the reverse — ja-WP 漫画版 「映画『神と神』を原作とした「破壊神ビルス編」は描かれた」 and 「連載開始時の「破壊神ビルス編」は劇場版『神と神』のダイジェストのような内容であった」; the film's own article from the other side 「『ドラゴンボール超』においては、本作を原作とした「破壊神ビルス編」として、テレビシリーズ複数話分にリメイク・再構成している」; en-WP 'both films would eventually be adapted into the first and second story arcs of Dragon Ball Super, which expanded upon the plot of both films'. (AniList encodes the same direction: the ADAPTATION edge belongs to the MANGA node, 86508 → 14837.) WHAT THE MANGA CHANGED (T28, for the note): it ADDS the Champa/Vados debut — the pair hunting the Super Dragon Balls behind Beerus' back, destroying the Frieza-Force officer Garana, caught watching the Kaiōshin through the crystal ball (ja-WP 相違点（破壊神ビルス編）; the scene is in Kanzenshuu's arc synopsis) — the seed of the next arc, which the film knows nothing about; it REWRITES the climax — on film Goku's Super Saiyan God expires mid-fight, Chi-Chi's prayer and his friends' voices flash him back into it to cancel Beerus' last sphere, Beerus names him the loser and reasons that his body absorbed the god power, while in the manga the form never cancels, Whis intervenes the instant the attack is nullified and calls it 「今回は引き分け」, and no absorption is ever stated; and it CUTS the film's party act — ch 2 ends with Beerus and Whis arriving above Earth and ch 3 opens on a fight already lost, the pudding surviving only as a line of dialogue, so Vegeta's placating dance, the pudding quarrel and Buu vs Beerus exist on film and on TV (our ep 6) and nowhere in print. STANDING — CANON under T30, and the catalog's own applied rulings point the same way: dragon-ball-super is the ruled PARALLEL series (I40), where the test is FROM THE OUTLINE OR NOT and canon = the story in ANY official telling; this film is the arc's first telling and the thing both later tellings realize. Sean has already typed the film's own material canon on this shelf — ep 6, the birthday-party sequence that exists in the FILM and not in the manga's pages, was ruled canon (timeline B) on 2026-09-05 with side_source{the film} kept and no adoption. The competing reading is PROTOCOL-extras' own sentence, which names this work; see flag 1.

chapters_adapted.note: CORRESPONDENCE, NOT ADAPTATION (A46 — this owner is parallel): the film's story is 破壊神ビルス編 = DBS manga ch 1-4 (其之一 16pp / 其之二 15pp / 其之三 15pp / 其之四 19pp = 65 pages, V-Jump 2015年8月号-11月号, collected in vol 1 『第6宇宙の戦士たち』 = ch 1-9). The film PRECEDES all of it by 27 months, so it cannot be adapting these pages — they are where a reader meets this story inside the instrument, and the stored arc ruling (arcs.ts, 'Battle of Gods', shared, eps 1-14 ↔ ch 1-4) already says exactly that. The same story is our TV rows 1-14 (dragonball.fandom's arc infobox says anime 1-15 and ja-WP's arc header runs 1-18 — an arc-boundary variance, not a disagreement about the film's material; batch 20 wave 5 fixed the block at 1-14 for this catalog). The manga's four chapters are a DIGEST: 65 pages against an 85-minute film and fourteen episodes, one scene the film does not have (Champa and Vados) and a different closing beat (Whis' draw).

position.why: 0.5 — before ep 1 — is right in both orders at once, which is worth saying out loud: it is the RELEASE order (film 2013-03-30; manga ch 1 2015-06-20; TV ep 1 2015-07-05) and it is the STORY order (the film's story IS the run's opening arc; there is nothing in the run for it to come after). It is the Mugen Train shape this programme has already ruled once (112151 at 26.5 — 'this work IS our rows 28-33 … a viewer takes one path or the other'): a viewer takes the 85-minute film, OR our rows 1-14 (ja-WP: the film 「リメイク・再構成」 across several TV episodes), OR the manga's 65-page digest — not all three for the story's sake. No other slot is defensible: 14.5 would put the first telling after the retelling, and anything later spoils a run whose opening fourteen episodes are this film. Position 0.x (before ep 1) is explicitly allowed by the ledger (E2).

flags_for_sean: FLAG 1 — THE STANDING IS A RULE FORK, AND IT IS THE ONLY REAL DECISION ON THIS ROW. PROTOCOL-extras.md names this exact work: 'A film the author wrote that the source LATER adopted (Battle of Gods → the DBS manga) is `filler` here with an `adopted` note — the adoption is the SERIES' fact (T26), never this row's standing.' That sentence applies the adaptation-owner test ('does the work adapt the owner's chapters'); dragon-ball-super is the catalog's one ruled PARALLEL owner, where T30 replaces that test with from-the-outline-or-not (canon = the story in any official telling; filler = studio padding no telling's story depends on). Under T30 the film is canon — the arc's first telling, stored as a SHARED arc (arcs.ts) — and filler here would contradict our own applied typing of the same material (ep 6, canon, timeline B, whose only source tie is this film). I deliver canon. If you read the protocol clause as binding on a parallel owner too, the row is filler and NOTHING else in this verdict changes: the chapters (1-4), the position (0.5) and the no-adoption posture all stand. One line either way.

FLAG 2 — NO ADOPTION, AND THAT IS YOUR OWN RULING, NOT MY OMISSION. THE ADOPTION QUESTION IS ALREADY RULED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. Sean, 2026-09-05 (the T26 adoption sitting + batch 22 wave 2, lib/rulings/episode-types.ts T30 pin on DBS ep 6 and lib/rulings/applied/batch-22.ts): 'NO adopted{author} (the bar is 脚本; this film's 脚本 is 渡辺雄介)' — Resurrection 'F' cleared that bar (原作・脚本 鳥山明), Battle of Gods does not. My research CONFIRMS the distinction rather than reopening it: ja-WP draws exactly the same line — 「正確には『神と神』では9割以上の原案・プロットを担当、『復活のF』では初めて脚本を担当した」. So no `adopted` record belongs on any of this film's three rows. The one thing the sitting did not weigh is the INCORPORATION prong (T26's second author test): the film's events ARE in the source line as ch 1-4, drawn by Toyotarou from Toriyama's plot with Toriyama checking every ネーム and redrawing pages of vol 1 himself (ja-WP 漫画版: 「ストーリー原案を務める鳥山明のプロットを基に、とよたろうがそれを膨らませて描き、出来上がったネームを鳥山が毎話チェックしている」). I do NOT propose reopening on it, for a reason that is structural rather than evidential: on a parallel owner the instrument for 'the same story in the other telling' is CORRESPONDENCE (A46) — which this series already carries as a shared arc plus per-episode correspondence rows — and the standing does not need an adoption to stand. If you ever did adopt it, the same act would also land on ep 6.

FLAG 3 — A46 ON THE LEDGER FIELDS. On a parallel owner chapter numbers are correspondence, never adaptation. I filled chapter 4 / volume 1 / chapters_adapted '1-4' because they are TRUE as correspondence, useful to a reader ('this story is DBS manga ch 1-4') and identical to the stored arc ruling; the related-works writer has no parallel gate, so they will be written as given. If you would rather the parallel shelf carry no chapter numbers, null the three fields — the facts survive in the note. Either way the note must say 'the manga digests the film', never 'the film adapts the manga'.

FLAG 4 — THE HALO NOTE'S DIRECTION IS BACKWARDS: the stored row reads 'adapts the series' own instrument: Dragon Ball Super (MANGA)'. The AniList edge behind it is the MANGA node's ADAPTATION edge (86508 → 14837 — the manga adapts the film; batch-20 verifier, research/batch20/verify/dragon-ball-super-w5a.md), the protocol's comicalization trap read from the wrong end. The ruled note should replace it.

FLAG 5 — THE PAIRED WORK, AND WHY IT IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE. Resurrection 'F' (AniList 20778) will reach this shelf too, and the stored arc table already distinguishes them: 'Battle of Gods' is kind SHARED (eps 1-14 ↔ ch 1-4) while "Resurrection 'F'" is kind SIDE_SOURCE (eps 15-27, the manga 「未登場」 — it skips the arc and only narrates its outcome in ch 5 and ch 32). So on the DBS shelf this film corresponds to real chapters and that one corresponds to none; and the adoption runs the other way round (RoF cleared the 脚本 bar, this film did not). Worth ruling both films in one sitting so the shelf reads coherently.

FLAG 6 — SIZING / T28, so it is not re-litigated: nothing in the film sits OUTSIDE this owner's story. The beats the manga cut (the arrival, Vegeta's dance, the pudding quarrel, Buu vs Beerus) are told in the run itself (eps 1-14; ep 6 is the party in full, ruled canon on the pages of ch 3 by the wave-2 verifier), and the manga's own additions (Champa/Vados; Whis' draw) are the instrument's variant of the same node. There is no anime-original share to weigh — the choice under flag 1 is canon-or-filler, never mixed.

FACTS CHECKED, NO REPAIRS: title, kind (movie) and air date 2013-03-30 agree with ja-WP (公開 2013年3月30日; 劇場公開版85分 / 特別版105分), en-WP and dragonball.fandom. AniList's GraphQL API returned 403 ('temporarily disabled') for every attempt during this task, so all AniList facts used here come from the context's staging or the batch-20 verifier's record — none is guessed.
